summary.headline: Suprajit Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 24% to INR1,070 crore and operational EBITDA 57% to INR129 crore, while standalone EBITDA was flat at INR60 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue hit a record INR1,070 crore (up 24% YoY) and operational EBITDA reached INR129 crore (up 57%). Global Cables and Mechatronics (GCM) drove the gain, with EBITDA margin rising from 5.8% to 12.6% after the global restructuring. Standalone margins were squeezed by raw material and wage inflation in ICM (margin ~15% to ~13%) and by delayed price pass-through in PLE (margin 6.7%, down 2.8pp); management calls both timing issues and expects recovery in Q2-Q3. Management reiterated FY27 guidance from the 25 May 2026 release.

financial_highlights.change: invested in mutual funds and bonds

segments.name: Global Cables and Mechatronics (GCM, formerly SCD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~27-28% reported, ~23% after adjusting for two months of SCS Canada/China tranche not in base; EBITDA margin 12.6% vs 5.8%. Management says 12%-plus is current, guidance 10%-12% retained.

segments.name: India Cables and Mechatronics (ICM, formerly DCD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~21%, broad-based across OEM and aftermarket; EBITDA up 4.2% with margin down from ~15% to ~13% on raw material and wage costs. CBS revenue up 110% and brake shoes/pads up ~80% off a small base.

segments.name: Phoenix Lighting and Electricals (PLE, formerly PLD)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 5.4%, EBITDA down 45%, margin 6.7% (down 2.8pp) on delayed aftermarket price increases; new prices now in effect. Ramp-up with a large US retailer; Middle East Trifa sales soft.

segments.name: Sensors, Electronics and Displays (SED)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 48%, EBITDA up 100%, margins close to double digits, led by digital clusters and electronic throttle grips. July was reported as the division's highest-sales month.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance from 25 May 2026 release reiterated: consolidated double-digit revenue growth; consolidated operational EBITDA margin 12%-13.5%.
GCM: double-digit growth and 10%-12% operational EBITDA margin (current margin is above this range).
ICM: EBITDA margin around last year's ~15%; PLE: around 12%; SED: around 10%, in line with last year.
Management expects standalone margin shortfall to recover by Q2-Q3; on full year, standalone margin within ~50bps of last year, with at most ~100bps downside as an extreme case.
Management said it will not change margin guidance until year-end, after the restructuring outcome is visible.
GCM expects strong double-digit growth in Q2 based on July trends; August is a seasonally weak month.
capex_capacity: SED: capacity expansion on a war footing; company is relocating out of current site for about six months into a larger leased premises, then rebuilding the plant as a multistorey electronics facility. Earlier plan was sized for about INR250 crore of business.
New STC R&D building on track for completion in Q3 FY27.

GCM: new product launches in China (one of the largest Chinese EV OEMs, about 25 cable projects won, 5-6 launched) and India (lines for a large US OEM building a resilient supply chain). Business wins across India, Mexico and China.
SED: about six launches in the plant this month and next, across instrument clusters, actuators/sensors and throttle position sensors.
US retailer PLE programme: store count expected to roughly triple or go 4x next year.
demand_pricing: Indian automotive sector grew about 22% in the quarter; passenger vehicle and 2-wheeler both grew at double digits per management.
Global automotive and non-automotive demand described as flat to muted; GCM growth attributed to new contract wins replacing lost business.
Pass-through: raw material increases largely recovered; wage increases (mainly northern region) being negotiated, with some customers agreeing and others still resisting.

Three large GCM contract wins announced about a month earlier: largest EV cable contract (USD 5m annual, USD 37m lifetime); European luxury OEM (USD 2m a year, USD 12m lifetime); Japanese OEM (USD 1.2m a year, USD 6m lifetime).
Management described the business as very competitive globally but consolidating, which may favour stronger players on margin.
Braking: CBS customers include TVS and HMSI; management says validation cycles are long for this safety-critical product.

qa_highlights.question: Were there one-offs or FX benefits in GCM margin, and is 12% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no material one-offs; margin gains came from restructuring, leaner operations, cost projects and top-line growth. It is at 12%-plus, but guidance of 10%-12% is retained and depends on product mix.

qa_highlights.question: Can SCS be disclosed separately for Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: No. SCS was disclosed separately only until March 2026; it is now folded into GCM as entities were merged or restructured.

qa_highlights.question: Was the GCM 27% growth flattered by FX or acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reported 27% overstates growth; excluding April-May from the second SCS tranche, growth is about 23%. The USD/INR rate has been stable at about INR95-96 over the period.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Last year's gains came from large favourable currency moves on loans, debtors/creditors and forward covers, plus a Morocco subsidy not repeated. Currency has been stable since March, so the Q1 figure is much smaller.

qa_highlights.question: What drives SED growth and the EV exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is in instrument clusters, actuators/sensors and TPS, across multiple customers, with ICE as well as EV demand. Mahindra throttle ramp-up used a rare-earth-free design. Management expects strong growth for at least 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin shortfall in ICM/PLE temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a timing issue: price pass-through is still being negotiated, with recovery expected in Q2 and Q3 and cost reduction under way.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for PLE run-rate and the European insolvency?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes are declining in the old business; the European insolvency is unresolved. Management expects more clarity in the next quarter and sees opportunities over three to six months, with US retailer business growing.

risks_watch: Standalone margin recovery in ICM and PLE depends on customers accepting wage and raw material pass-through; management said some customers are still resisting wage increases, mainly in the northern region, with recovery expected in Q2-Q3.
GCM margin of 12%-plus is above the 10%-12% guidance band; management said it will not revise margin guidance until year-end after the restructuring outcome is visible, and August is seasonally weak.
PLE volumes in the legacy business are declining and the European insolvency remains unresolved; management expects clarity over the next quarter and an opportunity over three to six months.

SED capacity: relocation out of the current site for about six months and rebuild as a multistorey facility, with the earlier plan sized for about INR250 crore of business; execution and interim disruption to watch.

Other income fell sharply YoY because prior-year currency gains and a Morocco subsidy did not repeat; the Q1 base is much smaller, and the GCM growth rate is partly flattered by reported (not constant currency) figures, with the 27% reported growth about 23% after excluding the second SCS tranche.

summary.management_tone: Confident on consolidated and GCM performance, with management calling the restructuring complete and the margin gains operational rather than one-off. More cautious on standalone ICM and PLE margins, which it attributes to timing, and it declined to give a separate SCS disclosure, a median price per unit, or a content-per-vehicle target.
